proof_audit: Stock is ex-dividend; physical drift mu is not expected total return mu+q. Dividend cash is explicit in self-financing gains. Product-rule S dDelta and cross variation are financed through bank-unit changes; no holding terms are discarded.

PDE coefficient comparison and converse funded hedge use localized C1,2 Ito on t<T, S>0. Vanilla analytic deltas are bounded on a finite horizon; GBM second moments verify the stated Q-L2 admissible trading class.

Constant lambda=(mu+q-r)/sigma measure is constructed on fixed finite horizon. Normal exponential moment proves normalization and conditional martingale property. Positive density gives equivalence. Product density and conditional factorization give independent shifted increments; continuity gives Brownian under Q. No general stochastic-lambda Girsanov theorem claimed.

Discounted total-gain process discounts each dividend at its receipt date. Reinvested-dividend stock wealth is distinguished from ex-price and uninvested cash. Q-L2 discounted gains prove the applicable pricing/no-arbitrage implication without unrestricted local-martingale expectations.

Upper and lower truncated lognormal integrals are derived by completing the square. Delta, Q exercise probability and physical probability are kept distinct. Formula derivatives verified via A phi(d1)=H phi(d2).

Terminal convergence uses Lipschitz payoff and GBM mean-square convergence; payoff kink needs continuity rather than terminal C1,2. Spatial limits use payoff probability domination and parity. Negative-rate upper bound is discounted strike, not strike.

Uniqueness is restricted to continuous terminal solutions, interior C1,2 and uniform at-most-linear growth. Compact state/time stopping makes the stochastic integral L2. Positive GBM paths make stopping converge to T; Doob supremum-moment bound supplies dominated convergence. No uniqueness claim for arbitrary growth classes.

Zero volatility is a distinct deterministic economy requiring mu+q=r for a positive live stock. Absorbing spot and expiry are separate branches. Delta at deterministic kink is unavailable; zero-spot reported derivatives are right-family limits rather than uniquely identified holdings.

Discrete cash dividends require price-jump/value-matching and a nonnegative-stock/payment model. A carry-equivalent yield is not asserted to preserve the terminal distribution. Coarse funded hedging has either sign of error and is not continuous replication or empirical validation.
